advances: In the intact branch, preserve every whole-label pair while routing an absolute half of every label through one collision-aggregated physical fresh-KKT edge ledger.  This gives two halfspace-dominated equal-mass, equal-first-moment measures, one jointly packed at the KKT targets, and closes the base-rank-at-most-two case by \(G\geq P_\cap/64\).  It also gives an exact Hall-cut criterion for a proportional pair-preserving localization of the fresh KKT stress.  When the criterion holds, the proportional field retains both affine-annihilation equations and a fixed positive normalized affine defect.  No high-rank terminal or universal Hall-cut assertion is claimed.
author: research-agent
proof:
We first construct the pair-preserving half-scaled family.  Labels with \(\eta_\sigma=0\) contribute nothing and may be omitted.  Fix a physical endpoint \(y\).  By (10), the total label-occurrence demand \(d_y^\eta\) is at most the total incident fresh-edge capacity
\[
 \sum_{k\ni y}\omega_k^b=\beta_y^b.
\tag{40}
\]
Distribute the finitely many demands \(\eta_\sigma\), over labels incident with \(y\), among the finitely many bins \(k\ni y\) of capacities \(\omega_k^b\).  A greedy fill gives nonnegative numbers
\[
 \lambda_{\sigma,y,k}
 \qquad(k\ni y)
\tag{41}
\]
such that
\[
 \sum_{k\ni y}\lambda_{\sigma,y,k}=\eta_\sigma,
\tag{42}
\]
\[
 L_{y,k}:=
 \sum_{\sigma:\,y\in\{a(\sigma),b(\sigma)\}}
 \lambda_{\sigma,y,k}
 \leq\omega_k^b.
\tag{43}
\]
This allocation is made after all physical source collisions have been aggregated in (9).

For a positive label \(\sigma\), abbreviate
\(a=a(\sigma)\), \(b=b(\sigma)\), and define its transportation coupling by
\[
 \pi_{\sigma,g,h}:=
 \frac{\lambda_{\sigma,a,g}\lambda_{\sigma,b,h}}
 {\eta_\sigma}
 \qquad(g\ni a,\ h\ni b).
\tag{44}
\]
Equations (42) give the exact marginals
\[
 \sum_h\pi_{\sigma,g,h}=\lambda_{\sigma,a,g},
 \qquad
 \sum_g\pi_{\sigma,g,h}=\lambda_{\sigma,b,h},
 \qquad
 \sum_{g,h}\pi_{\sigma,g,h}=\eta_\sigma.
\tag{45}
\]
Set
\[
 x_{\sigma,g,h}:=\frac12\pi_{\sigma,g,h}.
\tag{46}
\]
Equation (45) proves (12).  For \(k=\{u,v\}\), summing separately over uses of \(k\) at \(u\) and at \(v\) gives
\[
 \zeta_k=\frac12(L_{u,k}+L_{v,k})\leq\omega_k^b.
\tag{47}
\]
This identity counts two uses when one coupled triple has \(g=h=k\).  Finally,
\[
 \sum_k\zeta_k
 =2\sum_{\sigma,g,h}x_{\sigma,g,h}
 =\sum_\sigma\eta_\sigma
 =P_\cap.
\tag{48}
\]
This proves (11)--(14).  The argument is labelwise and does not invoke the partner involution, so loop labels are retained without modification.

We prove the geometric circuit and the target ledger.  If
\(\mathfrak p=(\sigma,g,h)\) is positive, then every endpoint of \(g\) and \(h\) has positive fresh load, so all points in (15)--(17) exist.  Original label endpoints have the same parity.  Since \(g\) and \(h\) are same-parity edges,
\[
 u\equiv a(\sigma)\equiv b(\sigma)\equiv v\pmod2.
\tag{49}
\]
Thus the bases of \(J_{\mathfrak p}^0,J_{\mathfrak p}^1\) are integral.  The points \(\widehat p_y\) belong to \(C\), so convexity proves that every midpoint in (15)--(17) belongs to \(C\).  Direct expansion gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 K_g+K_h
 &=\frac12
 \left(\widehat p_a+\widehat p_u+
 \widehat p_b+\widehat p_v\right)\\
 &=J_{\mathfrak p}^0+J_{\mathfrak p}^1,
 \end{aligned}
\tag{50}
\]
which proves (18), including all coincident-point and repeated-tag cases.

For each \(k\), choose \(F_k\) with
\[
 0\leq F_k\leq1,
 \qquad
 \int_{C_{m_k}}F_k=\vartheta_k,
 \qquad
 \int_{C_{m_k}}xF_k(x)\,dx
 =\vartheta_k\ell_k^b.
\tag{51}
\]
Equations (7) and (14) give
\[
 0\leq\mathcal G_m
 \leq
 \sum_{k:m_k=m}\frac{\zeta_k}{\vartheta_k}
 \leq
 \sum_{k:m_k=m}\frac{\omega_k^b}{\vartheta_k}
 \leq1.
\tag{52}
\]
This proves (19)--(20).

Fix a closed ambient halfspace \(H\).  At a physical target \(m\), retain from (19) only those edge packets for which \(K_k\in H\).  Their summed density is at most one by (52).  Its mass is
\[
 T_m^K:=\sum_{\substack{k:m_k=m\\K_k\in H}}\zeta_k,
\tag{53}
\]
and, if positive, its barycenter is a convex combination of the points
\(\ell_k^b\) in the convex fiber section \(H_m\).  It therefore belongs to
\(\mathsf M_{T_m^K}(C_m)\cap H_m\).  Accepted fact 6769574fc1bd9f8d gives
\[
 \operatorname{vol}_d(C_m\cap H_m)
 \geq\gamma_dT_m^K.
\tag{54}
\]
The same estimate is immediate when \(H_m\) is the whole space.  Summing (54) over distinct physical targets proves the first inequality in (23).

We next prove the companion domination with one physical source ledger.  For every \(y\) with \(\beta_y^b>0\), choose a half-mass witness \(B_y\) for the first membership in (5), and put
\[
 \Phi_y^b:=\frac{2\beta_y^b}{a_y}B_y.
\tag{55}
\]
It has mass \(\beta_y^b\), barycenter \(p_y^b\), and (5) gives
\[
 0\leq\Phi_y^b\leq\frac12.
\tag{56}
\]
Count all four tagged source slots of every positive coupled triple before orienting any atom.  The inner slots at \(y\) have total mass \(d_y^\eta/2\).  If \(k=\{y,z\}\), the outer slots at \(y\) created by uses of \(k\) at \(z\) have total mass \(L_{z,k}/2\).  Hence the total tagged slot mass at \(y\) is
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 T_y^{\mathrm{slot}}
 &=\frac12d_y^\eta
 +\frac12\sum_{k=\{y,z\}}L_{z,k}\\
 &\leq\frac12(d_y^\eta+\beta_y^b)
 \leq\beta_y^b,
 \end{aligned}
\tag{57}
\]
where (10) and (43) give the last two inequalities.

Assign to every tagged slot of mass \(x_{\mathfrak p}\) at \(y\) the density
\[
 \frac{x_{\mathfrak p}}{\beta_y^b}\Phi_y^b.
\tag{58}
\]
A positive slot has a positive denominator.  Equations (56)--(57) show that the sum of all tagged densities on \(C_y\) is at most \(1/2\).

If one of the midpoint atoms \(J_{\mathfrak p}^0,J_{\mathfrak p}^1\) lies in \(H\), at least one of its two tagged source points lies in \(H\).  Orient the atom to one such tag.  At each physical source \(y\), sum the densities (58) of the selected oriented tags and call the result \(\Psi_y\).  Then
\[
 0\leq2\Psi_y\leq1.
\tag{59}
\]
If \(T_y^J:=\int\Psi_y>0\), its barycenter is a convex combination of selected source points in \(H_y\).  The density \(2\Psi_y\) therefore proves that this barycenter belongs to
\(\mathsf M_{2T_y^J}(C_y)\cap H_y\).  Accepted fact 6769574fc1bd9f8d gives
\[
 \operatorname{vol}_d(C_y\cap H_y)
 \geq2\gamma_dT_y^J.
\tag{60}
\]
Summing (60) over distinct physical sources proves domination of the measure obtained from (22) with coefficient \(2\gamma_d\), and hence proves the second inequality in (23).  Repeated sources, coincident atoms, and loop tags were counted before orientation in (57), so none is reused.

Equation (48) proves both mass identities in (24).  Multiplying the circuit (18) by \(\gamma_dx_{\mathfrak p}\) and summing over all coupled triples proves (25).

For one physical target \(m\), equations (19), (51), and (26) give
\[
 \int_{C_m}\mathcal G_m=t_m,
 \qquad
 \int_{C_m}x\mathcal G_m(x)\,dx=t_mq_m.
\tag{61}
\]
This proves the first conclusion in (27); the second is (14).  In particular, \(a_m\geq t_m\) whenever \(t_m>0\).

Assume the base support in (28) has affine dimension at most two, and put
\[
 A:=\operatorname{aff}\{m:t_m>0\},
 \qquad
 I_+:=\{z:a_z>0\},
 \qquad
 W:=\sum_{z\in I_+}a_z,
\tag{62}
\]
\[
 B:=\operatorname{aff}(I_+\cap A),
 \qquad
 q:=\dim B\leq2,
 \qquad
 W_A:=\sum_{z\in I_+\cap A}a_z.
\tag{63}
\]
Equation (61) gives
\[
 W_A\geq\sum_mt_m=P_\cap,
 \qquad
 W\geq P_\cap.
\tag{64}
\]
The support-free rank-at-most-two complete-core theorem of accepted fact 8aac56c49321466c gives
\[
 G\geq\frac1{64}\min\{W,2^{n-q}W_A\}.
\tag{65}
\]
Since \(q\leq n\), equations (64)--(65) prove (28).

Both measures in (21)--(22) are nonzero, have mass \(\gamma_dP_\cap\), and satisfy (23).  Apply the dominated-measure residual theorem of accepted fact be359f8a6c628483 to each one separately, using exactly the ranks in (29)--(30), and multiply its depth bounds by \(2^n\).  This proves the two inequalities in (31).  No addition of the two depth witnesses is used.

It remains to prove the Hall criterion and the conditional KKT conclusions.  Equation (10) gives
\[
 P_\cap
 =\frac12\sum_yd_y^\eta
 \leq\frac12\sum_y\beta_y^b
 =\Omega_b,
\tag{66}
\]
where the last equality double-counts the two distinct endpoints of every fresh edge.  Thus (32) is well defined.

Suppose first that (33) holds.  For a vertex-edge incidence \(y\in k\), define \(o_{y,k}\) as the total \(\overline x\)-mass of coupled triples which use \(k\) in the slot belonging to label endpoint \(y\).  Then
\[
 o_{u,k}+o_{v,k}=\alpha\omega_k^b
 \quad(k=\{u,v\}),
 \qquad
 \sum_{k\ni y}o_{y,k}=\delta_y.
\tag{67}
\]
For a vertex set \(S\), summing the second equality in (67) over \(S\) counts every internal edge with its full first equality and all cut-edge contributions nonnegatively.  Therefore
\[
 \frac12\sum_{y\in S}d_y^\eta
 =\sum_{y\in S}\delta_y
 \geq\alpha\sum_{k\subseteq S}\omega_k^b.
\tag{68}
\]
This proves (34).

Conversely, assume (34).  Put
\[
 \overline\omega_k:=\alpha\omega_k^b,
 \qquad
 \mathcal B:=
 \left\{
 x\in\mathbb R^V:
 \begin{array}{l}
 x_y=\sum_{k\ni y}o_{y,k},\quad o_{y,k}\geq0,\\
 o_{u,k}+o_{v,k}=\overline\omega_k
 \quad(k=\{u,v\})
 \end{array}
 \right\},
\tag{69}
\]
where \(V\) is the finite fresh-edge vertex set.  The set \(\mathcal B\) is a nonempty compact convex set, the Minkowski sum over edges of the line segments
\[
 \overline\omega_k\operatorname{conv}\{\mathbf e_u,\mathbf e_v\}.
\tag{70}
\]
Its support function is
\[
 h_{\mathcal B}(z)
 =\sum_{k=\{u,v\}}\overline\omega_k
 \max\{z_u,z_v\}.
\tag{71}
\]
We claim that \(\delta:=(\delta_y)_y\in\mathcal B\).  Both \(\delta\) and every point of \(\mathcal B\) have coordinate sum \(P_\cap\).  It is therefore enough, by finite-dimensional separation, to prove
\[
 \sum_yz_y\delta_y
 \leq h_{\mathcal B}(z)
 \qquad(z\in\mathbb R^V).
\tag{72}
\]
Adding a constant to every coordinate of \(z\) changes both sides of (72) by the same constant times \(P_\cap\).  Assume consequently that \(\min_yz_y=0\).  For \(t\geq0\), put
\[
 S_t:=\{y:z_y\geq t\}.
\tag{73}
\]
Apply (34) to \(V\setminus S_t\), and use the equal totals
\(\sum_k\overline\omega_k=\sum_y\delta_y=P_\cap\).  It gives
\[
 \delta(S_t)
 \leq
 \sum_{k:\,k\cap S_t\ne\varnothing}\overline\omega_k.
\tag{74}
\]
The layer-cake identities now yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_yz_y\delta_y
 &=\int_0^\infty\delta(S_t)\,dt\\
 &\leq
 \int_0^\infty
 \sum_{k:\,k\cap S_t\ne\varnothing}
 \overline\omega_k\,dt\\
 &=\sum_{k=\{u,v\}}\overline\omega_k
 \max\{z_u,z_v\}
 =h_{\mathcal B}(z).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{75}
\]
This proves (72), hence \(\delta\in\mathcal B\).  Choose ownership numbers \(o_{y,k}\) representing \(\delta\) as in (69).

At each physical endpoint \(y\), the bins \(o_{y,k}\), \(k\ni y\), have total capacity
\(\delta_y=d_y^\eta/2\).  Greedily allocate every half-label occurrence demand \(\eta_\sigma/2\) into these bins.  This gives
\[
 \overline\lambda_{\sigma,y,k}\geq0,
 \qquad
 \sum_{k\ni y}\overline\lambda_{\sigma,y,k}
 =\frac{\eta_\sigma}{2},
\tag{76}
\]
\[
 \sum_{\sigma:\,y\in\{a(\sigma),b(\sigma)\}}
 \overline\lambda_{\sigma,y,k}
 =o_{y,k}.
\tag{77}
\]
For a positive label, define
\[
 \overline x_{\sigma,g,h}
 :=\frac{
 2\overline\lambda_{\sigma,a(\sigma),g}
 \overline\lambda_{\sigma,b(\sigma),h}}
 {\eta_\sigma}.
\tag{78}
\]
Equations (76) give both marginals in (77) and
\[
 \sum_{g,h}\overline x_{\sigma,g,h}
 =\frac{\eta_\sigma}{2}.
\tag{79}
\]
Summing the two edge slots and using (67), (69), and (77) gives exact edge use
\[
 \sum_{\sigma,g,h}\overline x_{\sigma,g,h}
 \left(\mathbf1_{\{g=k\}}+\mathbf1_{\{h=k\}}\right)
 =o_{u,k}+o_{v,k}
 =\alpha\omega_k^b.
\tag{80}
\]
This proves (33), and hence the equivalence.

The dual equations in accepted fact 6496cb3b0fd44f9d are exactly (35).  Positive homogeneity of support functions and (36) give every conclusion in (37).  Thus the proportional pair-preserving physical ledger preserves the full fresh KKT affine-annihilation, not merely its scalar loads.

Finally, accepted fact 6e66cd69e25232b7, applied to the same fresh KKT optimizer and the same points \(p_y^b\), gives the edge-average defect retention
\[
 \inf_s\sum_k\omega_k^b
 \|\ell_k^b-s(m_k)\|_{D_k}
 \geq\Delta_C(b).
\tag{81}
\]
Because \(b\geq\omega^b\), the definition of weighted affine defect gives
\[
 \Delta_C(b)
 =\min_s\sum_kb_k\operatorname{dist}_{D_k}(s(m_k),L_k)
 \geq
 \min_s\sum_k\omega_k^b
 \operatorname{dist}_{D_k}(s(m_k),L_k)
 =\Delta_C(\omega^b).
\tag{82}
\]
Accepted fact 6bfe50fed9a5540b gives
\[
 \frac{\Delta_C(\omega^b)}{\Omega_b}
 >\frac{95}{97}\delta_*=\delta_0.
\tag{83}
\]
Multiply (81)--(83) by
\(\alpha=P_\cap/\Omega_b\).  The infimum scales by the same positive constant, and this proves (39).  Every asserted conclusion is now established.  The proof neither assumes the Hall cuts nor converts the conditional high-rank defect into a terminal.
statement:
Retain one common canonical intact instance of accepted facts e6cf877c81ebffb9, 6bfe50fed9a5540b, 6496cb3b0fd44f9d, and 6e66cd69e25232b7.  Thus \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) is the common convex body, and
\[
 C_y:=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:(y,x)\in C\},
 \qquad
 a_y:=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_y),
 \qquad
 \gamma_d:=\left(\frac d{d+1}\right)^d.
\tag{1}
\]
Let \(\mu_C\) be the mixed-volume measure, and put
\[
 G:=\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{core}}(C),
 \qquad
 D:=2^nh_{\max}(C).
\tag{2}
\]
The genuinely recomputed completed submatching and its fresh gauge-load-minimal KKT optimizer are
\[
 Q:=\sum_kr_k>0,
 \qquad
 0\leq\omega_k^b\leq b_k\leq r_k,
 \qquad
 \Omega_b:=\sum_k\omega_k^b>0,
 \qquad
 \beta_y^b:=\sum_{k\ni y}\omega_k^b.
\tag{3}
\]
Every positive fresh edge \(k=\{u,v\}\) is off-diagonal and same-parity.  Retain
\[
 m_k:=\frac{u+v}{2}\in\mathbb Z^n,
 \qquad
 \vartheta_k:=
 2^{-(d+1)}\left(a_u^{1/d}+a_v^{1/d}\right)^d,
\tag{4}
\]
and, for every positive-volume source fiber and every positive edge, retain
\[
 c_y:=\frac1{a_y}\int_{C_y}x\,dx,
 \qquad
 \mathcal K_y:=\mathsf M_{a_y/2}(C_y),
 \qquad
 D_y:=\mathcal K_y-c_y,
\tag{4a}
\]
\[
 \overline c_k:=\frac{c_u+c_v}{2},
 \qquad
 D_k:=\frac12(D_u+D_v),
 \qquad
 L_k:=\overline c_k+D_k
 =\frac12(\mathcal K_u+\mathcal K_v).
\tag{4b}
\]
Retain also the fresh endpoint points
\[
 p_y^b\in
 \mathsf M_{a_y/2}(C_y)\cap
 \mathsf M_{\beta_y^b}(C_y)
 \qquad(\beta_y^b>0),
 \qquad
 \beta_y^b\leq\frac{a_y}{4},
\tag{5}
\]
and
\[
 \ell_k^b:=\frac{p_u^b+p_v^b}{2}
 \in\mathsf M_{\vartheta_k}(C_{m_k}).
\tag{6}
\]
The one physical target ledger is
\[
 \sum_{k:m_k=m}\frac{\omega_k^b}{\vartheta_k}\leq1
 \qquad(m\in\mathbb Z^n).
\tag{7}
\]

Retain the intact whole labels of accepted fact e6cf877c81ebffb9.  Every label \(\sigma\) has distinct physical endpoints \(a(\sigma),b(\sigma)\), original weight \(\widehat\theta_\sigma>0\), and completion ratios \(q_y\).  Put
\[
 \eta_\sigma:=
 \widehat\theta_\sigma
 \min\{q_{a(\sigma)},q_{b(\sigma)}\},
 \qquad
 P_\cap:=\sum_\sigma\eta_\sigma>0,
\tag{8}
\]
\[
 d_y^\eta:=
 \sum_{\sigma:\,y\in\{a(\sigma),b(\sigma)\}}\eta_\sigma.
\tag{9}
\]
Then
\[
 d_y^\eta\leq\beta_y^b,
 \qquad
 \sum_yd_y^\eta=2P_\cap.
\tag{10}
\]
In intact Alternative 1 one additionally has \(P_\cap\geq Q/800\), but the constructions below require only \(P_\cap>0\) and (10).

There is a finite family of nonnegative pair-preserving weights
\[
 x_{\sigma,g,h}\geq0
 \qquad
 \bigl(g\ni a(\sigma),\ h\ni b(\sigma)\bigr)
\tag{11}
\]
such that
\[
 \boxed{\sum_{g,h}x_{\sigma,g,h}=\frac{\eta_\sigma}{2}}
 \qquad(\eta_\sigma>0).
\tag{12}
\]
For a fresh edge \(k\), define its physical use, with both endpoint slots and every repeated use counted, by
\[
 \zeta_k:=
 \sum_{\sigma,g,h}x_{\sigma,g,h}
 \left(\mathbf1_{\{g=k\}}+\mathbf1_{\{h=k\}}\right).
\tag{13}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{0\leq\zeta_k\leq\omega_k^b,}
 \qquad
 \boxed{\sum_k\zeta_k=P_\cap.}
\tag{14}
\]
No label is discarded, split from its other endpoint, or reclassified.  In particular, (11)--(14) retain the full mass of every loop label after the common factor \(1/2\).

Put
\[
 \widehat p_y:=(y,p_y^b),
 \qquad
 K_k:=(m_k,\ell_k^b)
 =\frac{\widehat p_u+\widehat p_v}{2}
 \quad(k=\{u,v\}).
\tag{15}
\]
For a positive coupled triple
\[
 \mathfrak p=(\sigma,g,h),
 \qquad
 g=\{a(\sigma),u\},
 \qquad
 h=\{b(\sigma),v\},
\tag{16}
\]
define
\[
 J_{\mathfrak p}^0:=
 \frac{\widehat p_{a(\sigma)}+\widehat p_{b(\sigma)}}2,
 \qquad
 J_{\mathfrak p}^1:=\frac{\widehat p_u+\widehat p_v}{2}.
\tag{17}
\]
All four points in (15)--(17) belong to
\(C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\), including all collision and repeated-tag cases, and
\[
 \boxed{K_g+K_h=J_{\mathfrak p}^0+J_{\mathfrak p}^1.}
\tag{18}
\]

For every positive \(\zeta_k\), choose one representing density \(F_k\) for (6), and, at each physical target, put
\[
 \mathcal G_m:=
 \sum_{k:m_k=m}\frac{\zeta_k}{\vartheta_k}F_k.
\tag{19}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{0\leq\mathcal G_m\leq1.}
\tag{20}
\]
Thus all physical target collisions are aggregated in one density before any metronoid membership or halfspace estimate is asserted.

Define the two positive atomic measures
\[
 \nu_K:=
 \gamma_d\sum_{\mathfrak p}x_{\mathfrak p}
 \left(\delta_{K_g}+\delta_{K_h}\right)
 =\gamma_d\sum_k\zeta_k\delta_{K_k},
\tag{21}
\]
\[
 \nu_J:=
 \gamma_d\sum_{\mathfrak p}x_{\mathfrak p}
 \left(\delta_{J_{\mathfrak p}^0}+\delta_{J_{\mathfrak p}^1}\right).
\tag{22}
\]
For every closed ambient halfspace \(H\),
\[
 \boxed{\nu_K(H)\leq\mu_C(H),}
 \qquad
 \boxed{\nu_J(H)\leq\mu_C(H).}
\tag{23}
\]
Their masses and full first moments satisfy
\[
 \boxed{|\nu_K|=|\nu_J|=\gamma_dP_\cap,}
\tag{24}
\]
\[
 \boxed{\int p\,d\nu_K(p)=\int p\,d\nu_J(p).}
\tag{25}
\]

For every physical target put
\[
 t_m:=\sum_{k:m_k=m}\zeta_k,
 \qquad
 q_m:=\frac1{t_m}\sum_{k:m_k=m}\zeta_k\ell_k^b
 \quad(t_m>0).
\tag{26}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{q_m\in\mathsf M_{t_m}(C_m),}
 \qquad
 \boxed{\sum_mt_m=P_\cap.}
\tag{27}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \boxed{
 \dim\operatorname{aff}\{m:t_m>0\}\leq2
 \ \Longrightarrow\
 G\geq\frac{P_\cap}{64}.}
\tag{28}
\]

For \(i\in\{K,J\}\), define
\[
 A_i:=
 \operatorname{aff}
 \operatorname{proj}_{\mathbb R^n}(\operatorname{supp}\nu_i),
 \qquad
 \rho_i:=\dim A_i,
\tag{29}
\]
\[
 r_i:=
 \min_{s:A_i\to\mathbb R^d\ {\rm affine}}
 \dim\operatorname{span}
 \{y-s(z):(z,y)\in\operatorname{supp}\nu_i\}.
\tag{30}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 D\geq\gamma_dP_\cap
 \frac{2^{n-\rho_K}}{r_K+1},}
 \qquad
 \boxed{
 D\geq\gamma_dP_\cap
 \frac{2^{n-\rho_J}}{r_J+1}.}
\tag{31}
\]
Only the maximum of these two valid lower bounds is asserted.

There is also an exact criterion for preserving the fresh KKT affine-annihilation equations.  Put
\[
 \alpha:=\frac{P_\cap}{\Omega_b}\in(0,1],
 \qquad
 \delta_y:=\frac{d_y^\eta}{2}.
\tag{32}
\]
The following are equivalent.

\[
 \begin{array}{ll}
 {\rm (i)}
 &
 \text{There are nonnegative }
 \overline x_{\sigma,g,h}
 \text{, indexed as in (11), such that}\\[1mm]
 &
 \displaystyle
 \sum_{g,h}\overline x_{\sigma,g,h}
 =\frac{\eta_\sigma}{2}
 \quad(\eta_\sigma>0),\\[2mm]
 &
 \displaystyle
 \sum_{\sigma,g,h}\overline x_{\sigma,g,h}
 \left(\mathbf1_{\{g=k\}}+\mathbf1_{\{h=k\}}\right)
 =\alpha\omega_k^b
 \quad\text{for every }k;
 \end{array}
\tag{33}
\]
\[
 \boxed{
 {\rm (ii)}
 \qquad
 \alpha\sum_{k\subseteq S}\omega_k^b
 \leq\frac12\sum_{y\in S}d_y^\eta
 \quad\text{for every finite vertex subset }S.}
\tag{34}
\]
Here \(k\subseteq S\) means that both endpoints of \(k\) lie in \(S\).  Criterion (34) includes vertices with zero label demand, and therefore audits every fresh edge rather than only edges adjacent to the label support.

Let \(v_k^b\) be the fresh KKT dual vectors retained from accepted fact 6496cb3b0fd44f9d, so
\[
